 India sent a strong squad to these Asian Games and they have delivered the gold. They were put under pressure today, but their experience and composure helped them come out on top when it mattered. That brings us to the end of India’s Asian Games cricket campaign. But there is another Indian team in action right now, with the ODI side batting first in the third ODI against West Indies. Switch tabs and catch all the action from that game. Until next time, goodbye and stay safe.. Shreyas Iyer | India captain: If I have to use a word, I would say ecstatic as well because since the day we arrived in Japan, it was raining cats and dogs and we couldn't practice for almost a week. But the boys, the way they prepped themselves and also were doing their training on the side, we didn't complain, we didn't give any reasons. So that was a sign of a champion itself, champion team. And today was just a reflection of that. [On his emotions when Pakistan were chasing] Well, they were cruising pretty well and they got that momentum in between. I just wanted to see that I get that fifth (bowlers) over as soon as possible, finish it off, and then Bumrah was there, Washi was there, the lead bowlers, they wanted to come in as well. So I basically paced their overs pretty well. That's what I felt. And especially when the run rate is about 13 to 14, we know that the batsmen, they are going to take charge, and one wicket is going to change the momentum, shift the momentum towards us. So that's what happened, and that crucial wicket of.. I don't remember the name of the batsman (Ayub), but that changed the momentum. [On different players contributing to today's win] Exactly. When you're playing a final, you want each and every individual to step up and deliver, and that's what we witnessed today. Abhishek giving us that start, and then Tilak basically finishing off the innings, and then in bowling Washi taking the charge, Axar being himself all the time, and Bumrah, we know what he has got. So yeah, collective effort, and overall I would say comprehensive win. [On the celebrations tonight] Definitely, I mean I'm extremely happy, and all of us are just waiting to go back to the hotel. We've been on the ground for a while now, so yes, we haven't decided what we are going to do, but let's see. The dignitaries are making their way out to the middle with Jay Shah leading them. The three teams - Sri Lanka, India and Pakistan - follow them and stand behind the dias. The bronze medal is being presented to the Sri Lankan players. Now Pakistan's players are receiving their silver medal. Jay Shah is presenting the gold medal to the Indian team. India's national anthem is being played as the tricolor flag is being hoisted on the pole. The three teams along with the dignitaries line-up for the photographs. Some of the Indian players brought the tricolor flag onto the ground. The whole team took a photo with it and are now taking a lap of the ground to thank the crowd. Meanwhile, the stage is being prepared for the medal presentation. Stats by Roshan Gede Most sixes for Pakistan in a T20I innings

61 - Mohammad Hafeez, Bengaluru, 2012 17:03 Local Time, 08:03 GMT, 13:33 IST: How crucial was that partnership between Tilak and Dube? After India’s quick start, Pakistan fought their way back into the contest and looked set to restrict them to around 180-190. But the 62-run stand for the sixth wicket proved to be the difference, taking India past 200 and giving them the cushion they needed in the end. Pakistan could not match India’s powerplay effort. They lost a couple of wickets early and managed just 39 in the first six overs. Hasan Nawaz, dropped on 4, then gave Pakistan hope with an 87-run partnership with Saim Ayub. Nawaz kept going even after Ayub’s departure, taking the game deep and bringing the equation down to 52 from the final 3 overs. But India held their nerve when it mattered. Washington bowled an excellent 18th over, before Bumrah conceded just 11 in the 19th to leave Dube with 33 to defend in the final over. The all-rounder kept his composure and got the job done. Chasing 212 was never going to be easy, but Nawaz’s brilliant 96 ensured Pakistan stayed in the contest and caused a few jitters in the Indian camp. In the end, though, India held on to seal another win over Pakistan - their seventh straight victory over them in this format.
